items.title: Google Earth’s AI deepfake tool only lasted one day
items.summary:
Pompeii reimagined with Nano Banana 2 in Google Earth. | Image: Google	

Google has shut down Google Earth feature it launched Thursday that allowed users to edit satellite images with text prompts using AI. The tool essentially let users create AI deepfakes of the real world using text prompts; Digital Digging's Henk van Ess, for example, intentionally generated images adding things like refugees near the Mexican border and a bomb crater by a hospital in Gaza. On Thursday, Google's initial response to van Ess noted that images generated with Nano Banana 2 in Google Earth included a digital watermark and that the company prevented "image creation on harmful topics."

The NHTSA is investigating 1.2 million Tesla vehicles over suspension failure reports
items.summary:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is probing nearly 1.2 million Tesla vehicles after receiving complaints about a suspension failure that could cause "a loss of vehicle directional control," as reported earlier by Reuters. items.summary:

items.title: The ban on robot vacuums won’t make them safer, only worse
items.summary:
All future robot vacuums manufactured outside the USA (i.e., all of them) have been banned by the FCC. | Photo by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge	

No other gadget knows as much about your home as a robot vacuum. They map your space, learn your routines, and many now carry a camera and microphone into every room in your house. items.title: Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream is a quirky life sim that’s worth buying at this discount
items.summary:
Looking to start your own island paradise full of Miis based on family, friends, and celebrities, but don’t feel like paying full fare? Woot has Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream for Switch on sale for $52.99 (usually $59.95). Sort of like Animal Crossing, but more off-kilter, this unique game sees you building and managing relationships on an island of custom Mii characters. You’ll set up and decorate housing, discover what the inhabitants like and dislike, and watch as they interact with each other and form their own community. This discount is for the region-free international version (so it’ll work in all Switch consoles), and includes improved loading times for Switch 2 owners.
Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream

Where to Buy:

 $59.99 $52.99 at Woot

The second game in the series, Living the Dream adds a variety of new tools for you to build your island paradise, which folks have used to recreate simulacrums of celebrities, fictional characters, and real people in their lives. Once they’ve settled in, these characters will mingle in unpredictable ways. They may date, become platonic besties, argue, or possibly get married, frequently leading to situations that are as touching as they are funny.
Other deals to consider
Woot has one-meter-long woven USB-C cables from Apple on sale in a variety of colors for $14.99 each (originally $19), with extra discounts if you want to buy two or three. The cables are rated for 60W of power, enough for iPad and iPhone devices, and transfer data at USB 2 speeds. You can use the coupon code APPLETEN to save an extra 10 percent once per account.
The Marshall Stanmore III speaker is on sale at Amazon for $249.99 (usually $399.99), matching the lowest price we’ve seen. This capable speaker features a variety of connectivity options, including Bluetooth 5.2, 3.5mm aux, and RCA jacks for your record player. The timeless, amp-inspired design will look right at home on a bookshelf or entertainment center, with bass and treble control knobs to tune your listening experience.
Life360 Tile Slim trackers are $30 for a pack of two at Amazon, just about half off their usual price and the lowest we’ve seen. Compatible with both iOS and Android devices via the Tile app, these credit card-shaped trackers can easily slide into a bag or wallet so you can easily find them, and have an SOS feature that will let you quickly call a friend or family member for help in an emergency.

The major labels propose rules to keep AI slop off the charts
items.summary:
Several record labels, including the big three - Universal Music Group, Sony Music, and Warner Music Group - have proposed rules regarding chart eligibility for AI songs. In short, they wouldn't be. 
The proposal goes quite a bit further than a labeling proposal put forth by the RIAA, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), SAG-AFTRA, and others. That would create a set of standardized labels for AI-generated and AI-assisted music. New York is suing Kalshi over claims the prediction market is running "an illegal gambling operation." Anthropic just realized several of its Claude AI models hacked into the systems of three different organizations during testing, acting on their own and without the company noticing.
